about: Macedonian in real, everyday sentences, with each one's words in Macedonian order.

words.ми: my (after a family word); to me
words.мој: my; mine (мојот: my, before a noun)
words.се: oneself; each other (се гледаме); are (they are)

concept.line: A verb's ending says who does it, so јас (I) and ти (you) are usually left out: живеам (I live), живееш (you live), живее (lives).

words.means: едно = one; еден = one; една = one

concept.line: сум (am), си (are), е (is), сме, сте, се (are) say what someone or something is, where it is, or where it is from: Јас сум од Америка (I am from America).
With close family, short ми follows the noun (сестра ми: sister my); elsewhere, forms of мој can come before a noun (мојот пријател: my friend) or stand alone (книгава е моја: book-this is mine).

words.means: имам = I have; имаш = you have

concept.line: A yes-or-no question can start with дали (Дали имаш деца?: whether / you-have / children), put ли after the part being asked about, often the verb (Има ли леб?: there-is / (question) / bread), or use question intonation alone; a question word such as каде usually comes first.

words.means: зборуваш = you speak; зборувам = I speak; зборува = speaks
разбирам = I understand; разбираш = you understand

concept.line: не goes before the verb and any short pronoun with it: Не разбирам (not I-understand).

words.means: живее = lives; живеам = I live; живееш = you live
одам = I go; одиш = you go; оди = goes

concept.line: A noun is masculine (лебот), feminine (куќата) or neuter (кафето), and the words with it match: мал, мала, мало (small).
